$comment: Prop scatter and batching. Every number the Meadows looks like lives here; PropBatcher.ts and Prototypes.ts contain no tuning literals. Moving this into a per-biome file is the M6 job, when a second biome exists to justify the schema.
$comment_batching: Props are batched by (family x spatial cell), NOT by terrain chunk. Per-chunk batching cost one draw call per chunk per family and measured 1576 draw calls against a budget of 150. A cell is sized to its family's own draw distance, so at most 3x3 cells of any family are ever resident and each is one draw call.
$comment_cellSize: cellSize == drawDistance is deliberate. The disc of radius R around the player reaches at most one cell in each direction when cells are R across, capping resident cells per family at 9 before distance culling. Larger cells mean fewer draws but more wasted instances behind the player; smaller cells invert that.

families.$comment: Sparse oak groves in grassland, GAME_DESIGN.md section 9. The meadow gets the occasional lone tree, the grove gets a stand.
Kept as its own family so groves mix silhouettes.

Flower carpets are the strongest single colour accent in the reference shots, and one bloom per 87 square metres is not a carpet. Tightened from 3.4 and thinned less. maxSlope stays low so they read as meadow floor rather than hillside speckle.

The densest family by an order of magnitude, so it still gets the shortest draw distance. It used to stop at 44m against a 384m terrain view, which is why the meadow read as a bare golf course; the leaf-tuft source (36 tris, was 224) bought the range back at a third of the old triangle cost (D51).
families.$comment_density: minDistance is the binding constraint on lushness, not `density`: the achievable ceiling is about 0.318*density/minDistance^2, so no value of `density` could ever have thickened this. D51 cut the per-tuft triangle cost 6x and spent the whole saving on draw distance and on OTHER families, which is why the meadow stayed a golf course you could see further across. 2.1 -> 1.25 is roughly 4x the tufts. It is not lowered further because the Poisson pass costs 25 mask() calls per grid cell and each mask() is ~80 noise evaluations, so cost grows as 1/minDistance^2 and going under 1.0 turns chunk streaming into a soft hang.
families.$comment_scale: Scaled up alongside the density rise. Overlapping tufts are what turn scattered objects into ground cover, and enlarging costs no instances at all.

$comment_tint: Per-instance colour, multiplied onto each model baked vertex colours. The bases sit at 1: they briefly carried heavy corrections to rescue the Kenney kit foliage, which was the wrong fix for a bad silhouette (D65). What is left is the per-instance SPREAD, which is what stops a stand of trees reading as one stamped mesh. `value` is the half-width of the brightness jitter, `warm` pushes red up and blue down together, which is the axis foliage actually varies along.
